findings.issue: Export gate is asymmetric: the insufficient-cases guard requires riskCoverageComplete===true, and the recordPredictions gate at line 56 also requires riskCoverageComplete. A frozen review with riskCoverageComplete===false (any sampleCount) skips both guards and reaches workflow.export at line 59. If workflow.export does not independently re-validate coverage/sample floor (its source was not in scope), an under-covered or under-sampled review can be exported and subsequently attested.
findings.minimalFix: Make the sample floor unconditional (if(workflow.status(input).sampleCount<100) return insufficient_cases) and gate the final export on review.riskCoverageComplete, or add a comment pointing at the enforcing check inside workflow.export and cover it with a test.

findings.issue: readCurrentAssistantQualityAssessment swallows every error (including SQLite I/O failures, not just validation mismatches) and returns undefined. Callers cannot distinguish 'qualification revoked/not present' from 'database unreadable', so a transient DB fault silently downgrades to unavailable with no surfaced reason — in tension with the stated 'DB failures must surface' requirement, which is only honored on the invalidate path in AssistantAnalysisSettings.current(). Fail-closed, so availability/diagnosability only.
findings.minimalFix: Catch only expected validation errors (context missing, profile/scopes mismatch, digest mismatch) and rethrow DB-layer errors, or log the swallowed error with a non-secret tag before returning undefined.

findings.issue: current() performs two independent filesystem identity reads per call: actualIdentity() (fixed reader) and this.provider.readCurrentModel(). A config write landing between the two reads (or mid-write during either read) yields drift=true/unreadableProvider=true, which not only clears the provider but also invalidates the quality context and bumps the generation — a permanent revocation of an otherwise valid qualification caused by a transient race. Direction is fail-closed and matches the reconciliation design, but the blast radius (full re-assessment required) deserves a note.
findings.minimalFix: Acceptable as-is if intentional; otherwise retry the identity read once after a short tick before treating a null/mismatched read as drift, or document that any concurrent config write forfeits the current qualification.

findings.issue: configFingerprint is computed over the raw file bytes, so semantically identical configurations (whitespace, key reordering, comment-equivalent rewrites by tools) produce different identities and trigger spurious context invalidation and re-assessment. Additionally modelEpoch=floor(mtimeMs) inherits filesystem mtime granularity (1s on some filesystems); harmless for security because the fingerprint disambiguates content, but the epoch alone is not a reliable change signal.
findings.minimalFix: If spurious revocation is observed in practice, hash JSON.stringify of the normalized Config (with sorted keys) alongside the sorted transports instead of raw bytes; otherwise document that any config rewrite revokes qualification.

limitations: Static review only; I did not run tests, builds, or any commands, and did not read files beyond the pasted excerpts. The author's reported test counts (614 Desktop, 140 root, 50 stores, 31 offline counter, 2 admission, typecheck/build) are unverified by me.

Out-of-scope internals were assumed, not verified: LoopStore.transaction() nesting semantics vs BEGIN inside an open SAVEPOINT, syncAssistantQualityContext(null) generation behavior, workflow.freeze/export/import/revoke/readiness internal validation, qualityContextSchema, normalizeConfig validation guarantees, and how options.provider()/bootstrap wire provider.readCurrentModel to the fixed reader (AssistantAnalysisSettings.prepare enforces agreement at bootstrap, but the quality exportReview path relies on that wiring).

P2 finding on assistant-quality-product.ts:55 depends on workflow.export's internal validation, which was not shown; severity would rise to P1 if export does not enforce the coverage/sample floor itself.
Test source was not pasted and was not reviewed; synthetic-label tests and the absence of real human qualification (P3 remains OFF) are accepted as stated and were not independently assessed.

No live config, credentials, or real source data were used; identity-hash construction was evaluated only for design properties (domain separation, env precedence capture, error sanitization), not against real config corpora.
